title: Higher right derived functors vanish on injective objects
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category with enough injectives, $\mathcal B$ an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], $v:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ an additive (for instance left exact) functor with right derived functors $R^nv$ computed by injective resolutions [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. If $I$ is an injective object of $\mathcal A$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions], then $R^nv(I)=0$ for every $n>0$.

mathlib_searches.query: right derived functor vanishes on injective objects in positive degree

mathlib_searches.results: (F : C ⥤ D) [F.Additive] (n : ℕ) (X : C) [Injective X] : IsZero ((F.rightDerived (n + 1)).obj X), Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Abelian.RightDerived

line 153: lemma Functor.isZero_rightDerived_obj_injective_succ, proved from the resolution InjectiveResolution.self X; Functor.rightDerived (line 110) is the homology of F applied to a chosen injective resolution (isoRightDerivedObj, line 114), as in def-sp-left-exact-additive

mathlib_match.how: exact: for F := v (additive), n+1 for n>0, X := I with [Injective I]; Mathlib's F.rightDerived n is the n-th cohomology of F applied to an injective resolution (InjectiveResolution.isoRightDerivedObj), i.e. R^nv of def-sp-left-exact-additive; HasInjectiveResolutions follows from EnoughInjectives (instance InjectiveResolution.instHasInjectiveResolution / HasInjectiveResolutions)
